newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn to sell rest of Lufthansa in fall.
newsitem.headline: Bonn to sell rest of Lufthansa in fall.

text.p: The German government Thursday said it will sell its remaining 36 percent stake in airline Deutsche Lufthansa this fall, as part of the $2.7 billion privatisation aimed at keeping a majority stake in German hands.

The government development agency Kreditanstalt fuer Wiederaufbau (KfW), which has acted as temporary trustee for the shares since December 1996, said it would also sell a 1.77 percent stake in the airline, which it has held for some time.
Dresdner Kleinwort Benson and SBC Warburg will act as global coordinators of the Lufthansa sale, Germany's second-biggest initial public offering to date, a statement said.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell will act as senior co-lead manager, with DG Bank and Merrill Lynch as co-lead managers.
The government said the make-up of the issuing consortium should ensure that at least 50 percent of the shares would remain in German hands.
This would be achieved by selling most of the shares in Germany. Ensuring that a majority stake remains in German hands has been one of the stumbling blocks in completing the flotation.
The European Commission has wanted assurances from Bonn that ownership of Lufthansa would remain with Germans.
International air law requires flag carriers to show that national shareholders hold majority stakes if they are to retain their rights.
